technology_name: FABRICATION METHOD OF VANADIUM MONOCARBIDE NANOSHEETS AS EFFICIENT ANODE CATALYSTS FOR SINGLE-CHAMBER MICROBIAL FUEL CELLS
institution: National Institute of Technology Calicut (NIT Calicut)
technology_type: Microbial Fuel Cells / Anode Catalyst Processing
problem_solved: Single-chamber microbial fuel cells (MFCs) struggle with low power densities and high internal polarization resistances because standard anode configurations lack sufficient electrocatalytic properties.
description: An advanced liquid-phase exfoliation methodology to process bulk vanadium precursors into highly uniform, high-surface-area vanadium monocarbide ($VC$) nanosheets optimized to serve as anode catalysts within microbial fuel cells.
applications: Bio-electrical wastewater treatment arrays, off-grid low-power environmental sensor batteries, organic waste bio-refineries, and clean energy generation research lines.
secondary_sector: Advanced Materials & Chemical, Water, Environment & Waste Management, Biotechnology & Life Sciences
